Long before plate-clad knights, warriors wore bronze helmets: Corinthian, Attic, Thracian, Montefortino and many more. They're forged on the anvil from a &6bronze double sheet&r.
Besides helmets, bronze and iron make antique cuirasses, greaves and hoplon shields. Look up Antique Legacy recipes in JEI.
quests.lost_light.armory.armet.desc.0: The armet is a closed knight's helm. A helmet blank forged from a steel sheet is welded to a second sheet to make a &6barbute&r. Then a forged &6visor&r is welded onto the barbute.
quests.lost_light.armory.armet.desc.2: Black, blue and red steel have their own armets: their parts are forged from sheets of those steels.
quests.lost_light.armory.armet.subtitle: Visor down
quests.lost_light.armory.armet.title: Armet
quests.lost_light.armory.armor_stand.des: Armor needs a stand. An &6armor stand&r holds not only armor but also rings, amulets and other trinkets from Curios slots.
And the weapons you carry are shown on your belt and back, so everyone can tell at once who they're dealing with.
quests.lost_light.armory.armor_trim.desc: &6Armor trim smithing templates&r turn up &ein the chests of ruins and dungeons&r. At a smithing table a template, armor and a material make a pattern, and not just for looks:
- bismuth: +2 armor; diamond: +2 armor and +2 toughness;
- sterling silver: +2 toughness and fire protection; silver: damage resistance;
- ruby: speed and step height; topaz: sprint speed; sapphire: swim speed;
- amethyst: night vision; opal: stealth; pyrite: thorns;
- lapis: more experience; gold: luck; emerald and rose gold: villagers like you more.
quests.lost_light.armory.arrows.desc.0: An arrow is a head, a stick and fletching. Arrowheads are &6knapped&r from flint, stone and gems, carved from bone, or forged on the anvil from a metal rod.
quests.lost_light.armory.arrows.desc.2: Fletching is feathers or paper fletching (paper and glue). Arrows deal piercing damage: bring something heavier against skeletons and trolls.
quests.lost_light.armory.arrows.subtitle: Point by point
quests.lost_light.armory.arrows.title: A Quiver of Arrows
quests.lost_light.armory.bastard_sword.d: A bastard sword blade is welded from a regular TFC sword blade and an ingot of the same metal, then fitted to a hilt. The forging bonus carries over.

Other Epic Knights blades are made the same way: claymore, zweihander, estoc, katzbalger. Copper, bronze, wrought iron and steel are the mod's own, and bismuth bronze, black bronze and the colored steels have their own versions.
quests.lost_light.armory.bows.desc.0: TFC Archery bows are made from a frame and a string. The frame is put together from sticks: smaller for a shortbow, larger for a longbow. A &6plains bow&r also needs leather.
quests.lost_light.armory.bows.desc.2: Bows differ in draw strength and range: compare them in the tooltip and pick yours.
quests.lost_light.armory.bows.subtitle: The bowstring sings
quests.lost_light.armory.bows.title: The Bow
quests.lost_light.armory.buckler.desc.0: A buckler is a small fist shield. First a &6shield brace&r is forged from a double ingot, then it's welded to a second double ingot of the same metal.
quests.lost_light.armory.buckler.desc.2: A buckler is lighter than a regular shield and pairs well with a bastard sword.
quests.lost_light.armory.buckler.title: Buckler
Nine TFC &6steel chains&r are woven into a &6chainmail sheet&r. The sheets make a torso and sleeves, which are then welded into a hauberk.
Chainmail holds slashing blows well on its own, and it's also the base for heavier armor.
quests.lost_light.armory.chainmail.title: Chainmail
quests.lost_light.armory.crossbow.desc.0: A crossbow stock is made from lumber, three metal rods are fitted to it, then it's strung. The stronger the metal, the better the crossbow.
quests.lost_light.armory.crossbow.title: Crossbow
quests.lost_light.armory.gilding.desc.0: A &6Gilding Template&r is made from a small steel plate and a gold ingot. At a smithing table, with the template and an ingot of gold, silver, brass or rose gold, steel armor becomes ceremonial.
quests.lost_light.armory.gilding.desc.2: The template can be copied: a template and a gold ingot make two templates.
quests.lost_light.armory.gilding.subtitl: All that is gold does not glitter
quests.lost_light.armory.gilding.title: Gilding
quests.lost_light.armory.hilt.desc.0: Knightly weapons are put together from parts: the blade or head is forged on the anvil, then fitted to a &6hilt&r or a &6pole&r.
quests.lost_light.armory.hilt.desc.2: A hilt is a stick wrapped in &6leather strips&r. The strips are cut from leather, like any leatherwork. Two hilts make a pole for lances and halberds.
quests.lost_light.armory.hilt.subtitle: A sword begins with its grip
quests.lost_light.armory.hilt.title: The Hilt
quests.lost_light.armory.lance.desc.0: A lance is made from a pole, a &6tuyere&r and a metal ingot: the tuyere serves as the socket for the point. Long and heavy, it strikes best from the saddle at full gallop.
quests.lost_light.armory.lance.subtitle: Let the tourney begin
quests.lost_light.armory.lance.title: Knightly Lance
quests.lost_light.armory.plate_armor.des: A knight's breastplate is made in two steps. First a cuirass body forged from a double sheet is welded to shoulder pads, making a &6half armor&r. Then forged &6plate arms&r are welded onto it.
Plate is the best protection in this world, and the heaviest. There are other styles too: Gothic, Maximilian, Kastenbrust, jousting. Their parts are forged from steel as well.
quests.lost_light.armory.title: Armory
quests.lost_light.beneath.agonizing_fert: Pure essences of Death, Destruction, Decay, Sorrow and Flame are found in fortress and bastion chests. Each one is a fertilizer for soul farmland on its own, and all five together make &6Agonizing Fertilizer&r.
The &6Ancient Altar&r is made from blackstone, gold and black sand. Place a blank &6Lost Page&r on it and click with a gem: the page reveals its cost, reward and punishment.
The cost is laid out on other altars on the same level within 5 blocks, then you click the altar with the page. Don't put out extra: excess may be consumed too. In the Overworld the reward is halved.
quests.lost_light.beneath.burpflower.des: The &6Burpflower&r grows all over the Nether and can put a helpful curse on blocks. Place a sulfur block behind it: the flower charges, turns yellow, burps loudly and lets out sulfur smoke in the direction it faces.
The smoke turns nether bricks into &6hellbricks&r, charcoal piles into cursecoal piles, and adds decay to soul farmland.
&cCareful:&r iron and steel explode on contact with sulfur.
quests.lost_light.beneath.cursed_hide.de: Hoglins and striders drop &6Cursed Hide&r. On its own it's useless, but flux and white dye cleanse it into a large raw hide.
The Nether is also home to the &6Red Elk&r: take a good look at one.
quests.lost_light.beneath.cursed_hide.su: Even the beasts are cursed here
quests.lost_light.beneath.fortresses.des: The Nether holds &efortresses, bastions, piglin camps and lost cities&r. Blazes, wither skeletons and piglins live there.
Fortress and bastion chests hold &6Lost Pages&r and &6pure essences&r. Piglins trade gold for odds and ends, &6Ender Pearls&r among them.
quests.lost_light.beneath.gateway.desc.0: Beneath the world lies another one: cursed, hot and rich. Two paths lead there.
quests.lost_light.beneath.gateway.desc.2: The old path is a frame of &6obsidian&r lit with &6flint and steel&r (a flint and a steel ingot). Obsidian is made by putting a magma block into a barrel of water.
quests.lost_light.beneath.gateway.desc.4: The path of sacrifice is in the &dfield guide&r: hold a &6scythe&r, lay out seven offerings nearby (skulls, anvils, placed blocks of gold or black steel, ingots of pig iron or black steel) and kill a pig, a goat or a sheep next to them. A portal will open, but the underworld will invade your world for a while.
quests.lost_light.beneath.gateway.title: The Gates Below
quests.lost_light.beneath.hellforge.desc: The &6Hellforge&r is a huge forge: lots of fuel, lots of room and fierce heat. It's built from 21 &6hellbricks&r, with lava fed into its four corners through &6blackstone aqueducts&r.
The 3x3 center is filled with cursecoal piles and lit. Fuel and things to heat go into the same slots, so be careful what you put in. The layout is in the &dfield guide&r.
quests.lost_light.beneath.juicer.desc.0: You still need to drink in the Nether, and there's no water here. It doesn't evaporate in barrels, so you can bring a supply.
quests.lost_light.beneath.juicer.desc.2: A &6Juicer&r made of leather and a stick presses water out of the mushrooms that grow everywhere here, and out of fresh fruit. Drop mushrooms into its slot and drink.
quests.lost_light.beneath.juicer.title: The Juicer
quests.lost_light.beneath.lava.desc.0: Lava can't be carried in a wooden bucket: you need a &6blue or red steel bucket&r. Lava comes in kinds: regular, felsic, intermediate and mafic, and any will do.
quests.lost_light.beneath.lava.subtitle: Don't drop the bucket
quests.lost_light.beneath.lava.title: A River of Fire
Nether pebbles lie underfoot. Shape a pebble with a &6chisel&r to get a nether brick, and bricks with mortar make blocks.
Blackstone is made into bricks just like regular stone. If you have no blackstone, it can be made from soot and stone.
You can build even in hell
quests.lost_light.beneath.nether_ores.de: There are ores here too, and the &6prospector's pick&r works as usual:
- &6nether gold&r is common, and below the lava level there's more of it, and richer;
- &6cursecoal&r is a powerful fuel found &eabove Y 80&r;
- &6sylvite&r replaces basalt at any height; there's also pyrite and quartz.
Netherrack doesn't collapse, but blackstone, nether bricks and cobblerack do.
quests.lost_light.beneath.netherless.des: Create machines can make the Nether's gifts without it. A coal block polished with sandpaper becomes a coal rod. On a sequenced assembly line, the rod is filled with lava and pressed a few times over, and you get a &6Blaze Rod&r.
Quartz, soul sand, netherrack and other curiosities are made the same way. Look them up in JEI.
quests.lost_light.beneath.soul_farming.d: Soul soil can be tilled into &6soul farmland&r. Instead of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium it has five nutrients: Death, Destruction, Decay, Sorrow and Flame. They're shown while holding a hoe.
Each crop adds to its own nutrient and consumes the others. Nether crops can't die, but they don't grow without light. They're fertilized with sulfur, gunpowder, ghast tears and blaze powder.
The &6Ghost Pepper&r (Sorrow) is the Nether's edible vegetable. Crimson and warped roots, nether wart and the gleamflower can be grown too.
quests.lost_light.beneath.title: Beneath
The &6Unposter&r, made of crimson and warped lumber and a composter, feeds the mushrooms next to it. Put mushrooms, ghast tears or nether crops in it, and once a day it multiplies a mushroom nearby.
quests.lost_light.beneath.unposter.title: The Unposter
Bandits are rarely met on the road, but whole gangs live in camps in the hills. The kingdoms will be grateful.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.bandits.title: Highwaymen
quests.lost_light.bestiary.bears.desc.0: Black, grizzly and polar bears are the strongest beasts of the northern forests and ice. Stay away from a mother with cubs.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.bears.desc.2: &6Tip:&r bear fur softens hammer blows, but slashing weapons, an axe or a sword, cut through better.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.bears.title: Bears
quests.lost_light.bestiary.big_cats.desc: Cougars, panthers, lions, tigers and even sabertooths sneak up silently. Look over your shoulder often in warm lands.
&6Tip:&r big cats are weak to piercing weapons, so a javelin is the best choice. They resist crushing blows well.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.clay_golems.d: Kaolin and graphite golems roam where the ground is rich in these minerals. Smash a couple: something useful might fall out.
&6Tip:&r a graphite golem crumbles under crushing blows, while a kaolin one is better pierced: a hammer barely hurts it.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.crocodile.des: Crocodiles lurk by the banks of warm rivers and swamps. They say someone tried to befriend one. Don't.
&6Tip:&r crocodile scales resist piercing. Chop it or hit it with a hammer.
In TerraFirmaCraft weapons deal three kinds of damage:

Creatures have their strengths and weaknesses: some barely feel piercing blows, others crumble under crushing ones. Armor resistances are shown in its tooltip. Pick the weapon for the enemy: tips are in the quests of this chapter.
Not every blade is equally useful
quests.lost_light.bestiary.draugr.desc.0: Draugr are the dead warriors of ancient kingdoms: spearmen, archers, guards and knights. They follow a draugr lord. Lay him to rest and the army crumbles.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.draugr.title: Draugr
quests.lost_light.bestiary.dullahan.desc: In October the fey hide at night, and their lands are guarded by &6dullahans&r: dryads remade to hunt shades. They patrol the fey ground until dawn.
A dullahan is a fey creature too, so don't attack it. Befriend it instead: only in October the fey trade a &6Pumpkin Pact&r for a pumpkin laid in their ring. With it, a dullahan can be befriended.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.dungeon_dwell: Zombies, skeletons, spiders and creepers don't roam the surface: they hide in &ecrypts, dungeons, mines and abandoned buildings&r. Going there? Bring torches and a weapon.

&6Tip:&r shooting skeletons is pointless: arrows and piercing weapons don't hurt them, bring a hammer or a mace. Zombies, on the contrary, are weak to piercing. And a creeper is basically a plant: chop it with a sword or an axe.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.foliaath.desc: Foliaaths grow in jungles: carnivorous plants that pretend to be bushes and snap at passers-by. Approach from the side.
&6Tip:&r foliaath leaves soften slashing blows, so hit it with a hammer or a mace.
Defeat 250 creatures: beasts, monsters, outlaws, they all count. They already tell tales of you by tavern fires.
Your fame runs ahead of you
quests.lost_light.bestiary.light_spirits: Light spirits come only &eon the night of a full moon, one night in eight, under open sky&r: near standing water in the lowlands, or on the tops of the highest peaks. In October they come every night.

A &6wisp&r never strikes first, but hit it and it answers with slowness and nausea and is gone faster than you can follow. Catch its essence with a &6spirit seal&r: it's the only thing that wakes a spirit altar.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.not_again.des: You heard a quiet hiss behind you. You turned around. It was too late.
The creeper is the oldest trick in this world, and it still works every single time. Here's a souvenir.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.not_again.tas: Get blown up by a creeper
quests.lost_light.bestiary.orcs.desc.0: Orcs (warriors, raiders, berserkers, archers and shamans) come out of the badlands to plunder and burn. Meet them with steel.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.orcs.subtitle: Meat's back on the menu
quests.lost_light.bestiary.orcs.title: Orcs
quests.lost_light.bestiary.revenant.desc: A revenant is the body of a long-forgotten man raised by a shade. It remembers its arms: it carries a blade and a shield and knows how to use them. Revenants roam only &ein caves, and only in October&r.
Struck down, it falls into a heap of bones and rises again after five seconds, weaker each time. Break the heap and it rests at last, dropping its gear and a skull.
&6Tip:&r revenants are skeletons too: arrows and piercing weapons don't hurt them, bring a hammer or a mace.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.revenant.subt: Not all the dead rest easy
quests.lost_light.bestiary.scavengers.de: Hyenas and boars attack if you get too close. Boar meat, by the way, is very filling.
&6Tip:&r take hyenas with a javelin, and boars with an axe or a hammer: a javelin barely pierces a boar's bristles.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shade_ward.de: Shades are the least solid of spirits and the easiest to turn away. Salt, a jack-o'-lantern and a tiny skull carved from bone keep them at a distance. Walls and a shut door do it with less effort.

Best of all is a golden &6crucifix&r on the wall: no shade rises within 24 blocks of it, and those that come within 8 are shoved away. It's forged from a gold double ingot. Infuse it with light using a holy staff or a seal holding a light spirit, and it will burn shades within 16 blocks on its own.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.0: Shades are lesser spirits made of soot, rot and dead matter. Their domain is the dark of the night: after sunset they come out on the surface looking for the living.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.1: - the &6tall shade&r dashes in and claws;
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.2: - the &6hungry shade&r spits and steals your hunger;
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.3: - the &6creeping shade&r sneaks up and bursts into an intoxicating cloud;
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.4: - &6short shades&r are cave piranhas: frail and hurt by light, but they swarm and put it out;
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.5: - the &6plague shade&r lumbers on in a cloud of withering poison.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.desc.7: Fairies and dryads attack shades on sight, and on the night of a full moon the surface belongs to the light spirits and no new shades appear. But in October shades grow stronger and slip even into fey lands.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.shades.title: Shades
quests.lost_light.bestiary.spirit_seal.d: A killed spirit leaves essence behind, and it's lost unless something catches it. A &6spirit seal&r of fired clay holds one spirit: keep an empty seal in your offhand and land the killing blow yourself.
The dark essence of shades is the easiest to gather. At a spirit altar it becomes rituals, and a seal holding a light spirit infuses a crucifix.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.title: Bestiary
The trolls argued for a long time over how to cook you: roast you, boil you or just sit on you and squash you. They agreed sooner than you'd have liked.
Next time, keep them talking until dawn.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.trolls.desc.0: Trolls are spirits that have taken bare stone for a body. They live &edeep underground&r, where daylight has never reached. Hunchback trolls tear boulders from the ground and hurl them, and mage trolls cast spells and blink away when struck.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.trolls.desc.2: Sunlight turns a troll to stone on the spot. You could lure one to the surface, but everything it carried would be lost too. Killed underground, a troll often leaves good minerals.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.trolls.desc.4: &6Tip:&r trolls barely notice slashing blows, while a hammer or a mace hits them with full force.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.trolls.title: Trolls
quests.lost_light.bestiary.wargs.desc.0: Predators are rarer than tribesmen but more dangerous. Direwolves hunt in packs: if you hear howling, keep your weapon close. Wolves and direwolves count the same.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.wargs.desc.2: &6Tip:&r wolf hide resists crushing blows well. Strike them with a javelin, a knife or an axe.
quests.lost_light.bestiary.wargs.title: Wargs
quests.lost_light.bestiary.wild_tribes.d: This chapter is a hunter's journal: quests count kills of the right creatures. Only unlocked quests keep count, so finish this one first: it unlocks almost all the others.

The most common threat on the surface, day and night, are wild tribes: hunters, stalkers, bonebreakers, shamans and berserkers. Mercenaries serve anyone for coin. Predators are rarer, and bandits rarer still. And after sunset, shades come out of the dark.
&6Tip:&r tribesmen in hides shrug off piercing blows fairly well, while crushing weapons hit them a bit harder.
quests.lost_light.bosses.bluff.desc.0: Bluffs live in the dark caves &eof mountains and canyons&r: stony critters that pretend to be boulders. They drop a &6Bluff Rod&r.
quests.lost_light.bosses.bluff.desc.2: The rod is useless on its own, but the Sculptor takes it as the price of his trial.
quests.lost_light.bosses.bluff.desc.4: &6Tip:&r a bluff's stony hide shrugs off hammers, while piercing weapons hit harder.
quests.lost_light.bosses.bluff.subtitle: Rocks that bite
quests.lost_light.bosses.bluff.title: Called Your Bluff
quests.lost_light.bosses.crystal_thief.d: They say an ice crystal can be had without a fight: if the Frostmaw never sees you, the crystal can be carried off while it sleeps.
A good burglar needs no sword, only luck and very quiet steps.
quests.lost_light.bosses.eight_crowns.de: Eight kingdoms, eight kings. Should they all fall, no one will be left to dispute your right to rule.

Each castle stands in its own land: Valaria, Gardonia and Lancastia &ein hills and plains&r, Bohemia &eon plains&r, Galicia &ein hills&r, Caladria &eon the coast&r, Visgothia &ein mountains and highlands&r, Numeria &ein badlands and canyons&r.
quests.lost_light.bosses.frostmaw.desc.0: In an icy lair &ehigh in the mountains&r sleeps a huge white beast. While asleep it regains its strength, and once awake it breathes frost and hurls blocks of ice. The cold slows you down, so keep moving.
quests.lost_light.bosses.frostmaw.desc.2: A fallen Frostmaw drops an &6Ice Crystal&r: hold right-click to channel an icy whirlwind. The crystal recharges by itself while in your inventory.
quests.lost_light.bosses.frostmaw.desc.4: &6Tip:&r its hide barely lets piercing blows through, so javelins and arrows are useless. Bring a hammer or a mace: crushing damage gets through with interest.
quests.lost_light.bosses.frostmaw.title: Frostmaw
quests.lost_light.bosses.legend.desc.0: The Frostmaw, the Sunbird, the Sculptor, the naga, a king and the draugr lord have all fallen or bowed before you.
quests.lost_light.bosses.legend.desc.2: Few in this world can say as much. Your name will be remembered long after rust has eaten your sword.
quests.lost_light.bosses.legend.subtitle: Songs will be sung of you
quests.lost_light.bosses.legend.title: A Living Legend
The mountains hold more than ore. Creatures live there for whom an ordinary hunter is just a snack:
- the &6Frostmaw&r sleeps in an icy lair &ein any mountains&r;
- &6Umvuthi, the Sunbird&r rules the Umvuthana tribe from a grove &ein volcanic mountains&r;
- &6Tongbi, the Sculptor&r awaits the bold in a monastery &ein common and old mountains&r.
Find at least one lair. And don't rush in: stock up on food, bandages and a good weapon first.
quests.lost_light.bosses.naga.desc.0: The Naga is a winged sea serpent. It comes &eat night to high sea shores&r, no lower than Y 68, spits venom and dives from above. Stand near a cliff edge, and it may well knock you into the water.
quests.lost_light.bosses.naga.desc.2: A naga fang and an iron ingot make a &6Naga Fang Dagger&r: it poisons and strikes harder from behind.
quests.lost_light.bosses.naga.desc.4: &6Tip:&r naga scales resist piercing blows, while crushing ones hit harder. Bring it down to the ground and take it with a hammer.
quests.lost_light.bosses.naga.subtitle: A shadow over the surf
quests.lost_light.bosses.naga.title: Naga
quests.lost_light.bosses.regicide.desc.0: Each king rules from his castle, surrounded by knights and royal guards. Killing a king is a challenge to the whole kingdom: his subjects won't forget it.
quests.lost_light.bosses.regicide.desc.2: If you have a reason, or serve another crown, bring good armor and don't fight the whole guard at once.
quests.lost_light.bosses.regicide.title: Kingslayer
quests.lost_light.bosses.sculptor.desc.0: Those who come with a weapon instead of a rod are met by Tongbi with stone spikes and boulders. Whoever defeats him gets the &6Geomancer Staff&r and the geomancer's garb: beads, robe, belt and sandals.
quests.lost_light.bosses.sculptor.desc.2: &6Tip:&r stone doesn't take piercing well, but it cracks under a hammer.
quests.lost_light.bosses.sculptor.title: The Sculptor
Tongbi, the Sculptor, lives in a monastery &ein the mountains&r and doesn't care for fighting. Give him a &6Bluff Rod&r and he'll raise a stone tower 60 blocks tall.

You must climb to its top in under 400 seconds while the Sculptor gets in the way, crumbling ledges and hurling rocks. Make it, and you get the &6Earthrend Gauntlet&r: it lifts boulders, digs tunnels and raises stone pillars.
quests.lost_light.bosses.suns_blessing.d: Umvuthi can also be bargained with. Umvuthana masks sometimes drop from the tribe's warriors. Wear one and you'll pass for one of them.
The Sunbird grants the &6Sun's Blessing&r in exchange for &67 blocks of gold&r (TFC blocks are made from gold sheets). With it, an empty hand can call a sunstrike, a solar flare and a solar beam.
quests.lost_light.bosses.title: Bosses
quests.lost_light.bosses.umvuthi.desc.0: In a grove &eamong the volcanic mountains&r lives the masked Umvuthana tribe. Their chief Umvuthi, the Sunbird, calls down sunstrikes and fires a solar beam. When he's hurt, the tribe sends healers: deal with them first.
quests.lost_light.bosses.umvuthi.desc.2: Umvuthi drops the &6Sol Visage&r, a mask that never breaks. Wear it and right-click holding an Umvuthana mask to summon a warrior of the tribe.
quests.lost_light.bosses.umvuthi.desc.4: &6Tip:&r feathers resist piercing blows, while crushing damage gets through a little better.
quests.lost_light.bosses.umvuthi.title: The Sunbird
quests.lost_light.brewing.aging.desc.0: Any drink gets better if sealed in a barrel for a long time: after 24 days you get &6aged&r alcohol, stronger and finer than young.
quests.lost_light.brewing.aging.desc.2: Patience, traveller. Good things never come quickly.
quests.lost_light.brewing.aging.subtitle: Time is the best brewer
quests.lost_light.brewing.aging.title: Aging
quests.lost_light.brewing.beer.desc.0: Barley flour and water in a barrel. They say the best beer is brewed at a certain inn on the Great East Road: see if you can do better.
quests.lost_light.brewing.beer.subtitle: Like at the Prancing Pony
quests.lost_light.brewing.beer.title: Beer
Collect aged beer, whiskey and mead. In the cellars of a certain woodland king, the guards got so carried away tasting the wine that they slept through a dozen dwarves escaping in barrels.
quests.lost_light.brewing.cider.desc.0: Red or green apples and water in a barrel. A light and refreshing drink.
quests.lost_light.brewing.cider.subtitle: Spirit of the apple
quests.lost_light.brewing.cider.title: Cider
quests.lost_light.brewing.fine_wine.desc: Add sugar to white wine to make &6dessert wine&r. Add a &6tirage mixture&r of yeast and sweetener to make &6sparkling wine&r. Time to put a wine shelf in your cellar.
quests.lost_light.brewing.first_brew.des: Alcohol in TerraFirmaCraft is brewed in a &6sealed barrel&r: flour, fruit or sugar plus water, and after three days of fermentation the drink is ready. Barley makes beer, apples cider, rice sake, potatoes vodka, wheat, rye and maize various whiskeys, sugar rum.
Drinks warm you up and lift your spirits, but don't overdo it: a drunk man fears neither sea nor cave.
quests.lost_light.brewing.first_brew.sub: Fermentation is the oldest of sciences
quests.lost_light.brewing.mead.desc.0: Mead is fermented from honey and water. It is served in the royal halls of the horse-lords, and in any home that keeps bees.
quests.lost_light.brewing.mead.subtitle: As in the golden halls of Edoras
quests.lost_light.brewing.mead.title: Mead
quests.lost_light.brewing.rum.desc.0: Sugar and water in a barrel. Sugar is pressed from sugarcane, which grows in warm climates.
quests.lost_light.brewing.rum.subtitle: Fifteen men on a dead man's chest
quests.lost_light.brewing.rum.title: Rum
quests.lost_light.brewing.sake.desc.0: Rice flour and water in a barrel. Rice needs warmth and plenty of water.
quests.lost_light.brewing.sake.subtitle: Rice wine
quests.lost_light.brewing.sake.title: Sake
quests.lost_light.brewing.title: Brewing
Wild red and white grapes grow almost everywhere livable: from 0 to 30 °C and 125–500 mm of rain.
The vine needs a &6trellis&r: stack two posts, then two more two blocks away, and string jute fiber between them. Grapes flower in June and fruit in July.
quests.lost_light.brewing.vineyard.title: Vineyard
quests.lost_light.brewing.vodka.desc.0: Potatoes and water in a barrel. A strong drink for long winters.
quests.lost_light.brewing.vodka.subtitle: Keeps you warm in the cold
quests.lost_light.brewing.vodka.title: Vodka
quests.lost_light.brewing.whiskey.desc.0: Wheat, rye or maize flour and water in a barrel make whiskey, rye whiskey or corn whiskey. Any of them will do.
quests.lost_light.brewing.whiskey.title: Whiskey
quests.lost_light.brewing.wine.desc.0: Wine is poured into &6wine bottles&r of non-silica glass (volcanic, hematitic or olivine) and stopped with a &6cork&r. A cork is made by soaking treated lumber in limewater for a day.
quests.lost_light.brewing.wine.desc.2: Red or white grapes alone give red or white wine, a mix gives rosé. Wine keeps aging while the bottle is corked.
quests.lost_light.brewing.wine.subtitle: Red wine of Dorwinion
quests.lost_light.brewing.wine.title: Wine
quests.lost_light.brewing.wine_press.des: Put grapes in a &6stomping barrel&r and jump on it 16 times. Seal the smashed grapes in a barrel for 5 days to ferment, then press the juice in a &6barrel press&r. Four grapes make a bottle of wine.
quests.lost_light.building.chalk.desc.0: Chalk draws arrows and marks on any surface: handy so you don't get lost in a mine. A stick of chalk is made by soaking a &6chalk brick&r in a sealed barrel of dye.
quests.lost_light.building.chalk.title: Chalk
quests.lost_light.building.concrete_road: &6Dry concrete mix&r is made from base course and lime, then mixed with fresh water in a barrel. Pour the concrete from a bucket onto the base course: it spreads by itself and sets within a day.

While it's wet, nobody may walk on it: footprints are smoothed with a mattock. Pours wider than 4 blocks crack: cut control joints every 5 blocks with a mattock, or press bricks, flagstones or smooth stone into it.
quests.lost_light.building.decor.desc.1: - a &6Jar&r of glass and slabs holds liquids, food and even fireflies;
quests.lost_light.building.decor.desc.2: - a &6Notice Board&r displays a book or a note;
quests.lost_light.building.decor.desc.3: - an &6Item Shelf&r shows off a single item on the wall.
quests.lost_light.building.decor.title: Cozy
Storage Drawers hold lots of a single item and show what's inside. They're made from TFC wood. Upgrades raise capacity, and a controller links drawers into one storage.
A &6Label&r with an item can be hung on a chest or a barrel, so you don't have to search.
quests.lost_light.building.drawers.title: Drawers
quests.lost_light.building.furniture.des: Macaw's furniture is made from TFC wood: chairs, tables, wardrobes, kitchen counters. Roofs, fences and bridges too.
Double doors open together when you open one side.
A road is built in three steps: tamp the soil with a &6mattock&r, lay a &6crushed base course&r, then lay the surface. The base course is made from gravel, loose rocks and a hammer.
Tamped mud has to be covered with crushed base course first. Details are in the &dfield guide&r.
quests.lost_light.building.mattock.title: The Mattock
quests.lost_light.building.road.desc.0: The surface goes on top of the base course, and the better it is, the faster you walk:
quests.lost_light.building.road.desc.1: - &6hoggin&r (clay, gravel and sand) or a little gravel: +10%;
quests.lost_light.building.road.desc.2: - gravel tamped with a mattock (macadam), cobbles, stone or brick setts, flagstones: +20%;
quests.lost_light.building.road.subtitle: The road goes ever on and on
quests.lost_light.building.road.title: The Road
quests.lost_light.building.roof.desc.0: A roof starts with a &6frame&r of lumber and sticks; there are stair and slab frames too. Click the frame with a roofing material:
quests.lost_light.building.roof.desc.2: - wooden shingles for a shingle roof;
quests.lost_light.building.roof.desc.3: - fired ceramic or terracotta tiles for a tiled roof.
quests.lost_light.building.roof.subtitle: Keep the rain out
quests.lost_light.building.roof.title: A Roof Over Your Head
quests.lost_light.building.title: Builder
quests.lost_light.create.advanced_mechan: Enough playing around: time to build serious machines like pumps, smart chutes, gantries, elevators and rollers.
&6Create&r machines are available early in Lost Light. &6Andesite alloy&r is knapped from andesite rocks, just like stone tools, and later a deployer with a chisel can make it.
The stone it all starts with
quests.lost_light.create.basic_mechanism: Time for real automation. The &6andesite casing&r is the base of most machines: apply andesite alloy to a stripped log. The &6millstone&r grinds grain and ore, and the &6mechanical press&r flattens metal into sheets.
A mind of metal and wheels
Smart machines need brass. A &6brass casing&r is made like an andesite one, only with a brass sheet. An &6electron tube&r and a &6precision mechanism&r go into mechanical arms, smart chutes and mechanical crafters.
A precision mechanism isn't crafted but built by &6sequenced assembly&r: the part passes through several machines in a row. See JEI for the steps.
quests.lost_light.create.brass_age.title: The Brass Age
&6Shafts&r and &6cogwheels&r carry rotation from the source to machines. A large cogwheel changes the speed. You'll need lots of these parts.
quests.lost_light.create.cogwheels.subti: Cogs and what to do with them
quests.lost_light.create.cogwheels.title: Spinning Things
quests.lost_light.create.kinetic_power.d: Machines need power. The easiest start is a &6water wheel&r on a river, a &6windmill&r on a hill, or a &6hand crank&r if you don't mind the work.
quests.lost_light.create.kinetic_power.s: Water, wind or your own hands
quests.lost_light.create.kinetic_power.t: A water wheel, windmill or hand crank
quests.lost_light.create.mechanical_tool: The &6mechanical drill&r breaks blocks, the &6mechanical saw&r fells trees and cuts planks, and the &6deployer&r uses items like a player. Together they automate almost any job.
quests.lost_light.create.ore_crushing.de: &6Crushing wheels&r and the millstone grind TFC ore into powder. Powder can be melted, and the same ore gives more metal.
quests.lost_light.create.ore_crushing.su: More metal from the same ore
Roll up your sleeves: it's time to mine big! The &6vein finder&r locates deep deposits, and the &6drilling machine&r and &6extractor&r pull ore and fluids out of them endlessly.
quests.lost_light.create.steam.desc.0: Water and wind are too weak for big machines. Build a boiler of &6fluid tanks&r, pipe in water, put heat under it and attach a &6steam engine&r to its side. The bigger the boiler and the stronger the heat, the more engines it drives.
quests.lost_light.create.steam.subtitle: Isengard approves
quests.lost_light.create.steam.title: Steam Power
quests.lost_light.create.subtitle.0: Let the cogs do the work
quests.lost_light.create.title: Create
quests.lost_light.create.trains.desc.0: Lay &6tracks&r, place a &6station&r and assemble a train on it from &6train casings&r and any blocks. A train carries cargo and passengers across the world, and a schedule lets it run without a driver.
quests.lost_light.create.trains.subtitle: Faster than any horse
quests.lost_light.create.trains.title: Railway
quests.lost_light.enchanting.enchanting_: An &6Enchanting Table&r is made from a book, wrought iron sheets, red wool and obsidian. Obsidian is made by putting a magma block into a barrel of water.
Instead of lapis, the table is fueled by &6gem powder&r: gems are ground into powder in a quern.
quests.lost_light.enchanting.first_encha: Enchantments are paid for with experience and items. Each recipe has four slots:
- &6waste&r: bones and rotten flesh, compost and guano, mushrooms or spider eyes;
- a &6themed item&r: feathers for feather falling, salt against the undead, sandpaper for sharpness…;
- from level III, a &6precious metal&r: gold for luck, silver against the undead.
Recipes for all enchantments are in JEI. There is no Mending in this world.
You can only enchant with what you know. Knowledge is kept in &6enchanted books&r from chests: use a book and you learn every enchantment in it, while the book crumbles to ashes.
Learned enchantments stay with you forever.
quests.lost_light.enchanting.learn.title: Lost Knowledge
quests.lost_light.enchanting.master_ench: An item takes no more than &6three enchantments&r. A curse raises the limit by one, but no more than one curse fits.
Make an item with three enchantments.
quests.lost_light.enchanting.subtitle.0: Words of power and their price
quests.lost_light.enchanting.title: Enchanting
quests.lost_light.end.dragon.desc.0: The dragon here is stronger than usual and grows with the number of players. The crystals on the towers heal it and &6respawn&r over time, and a broken crystal leaves a poisonous cloud.
quests.lost_light.end.dragon.desc.2: Break a crystal in melee, and the dragon instantly loses a tenth of its health. Beware of lightning and explosions, and don't stand under the dragon.
quests.lost_light.end.dragon.subtitle: His name isn't Smaug
quests.lost_light.end.dragon.title: The Ender Dragon
quests.lost_light.end.elytra.desc.0: &6Elytra&r hang in the ships by End Cities. They don't take up the chestplate slot: they go into their own slot, and your armor stays on.
quests.lost_light.end.elytra.desc.2: Taking off with elytra is easier, and they can be trimmed just like armor.
quests.lost_light.end.elytra.subtitle: The eagles are coming!
quests.lost_light.end.elytra.title: Wings
quests.lost_light.end.end_city.desc.0: After the dragon falls, &6gateways&r to the outer islands appear. There stand &eEnd Cities&r: purple towers guarded by shulkers.
quests.lost_light.end.end_city.desc.2: To pass through a gateway, throw an Ender Pearl into it or fly straight through.
quests.lost_light.end.end_city.subtitle: Towers over the void
quests.lost_light.end.end_city.title: End City
quests.lost_light.end.ender_eyes.desc.0: An &6Eye of Ender&r is made from an &6Ender Pearl&r and &6Blaze Powder&r. Pearls are traded from piglins for gold and sometimes turn up in ancient chests. Blaze rods are taken from blazes in Nether fortresses or made on Create machines.
quests.lost_light.end.ender_eyes.desc.2: A thrown eye flies toward the nearest &eancient stronghold in the mountains&r. Sometimes it shatters, so make a stock: the portal frame needs 12 eyes.
quests.lost_light.end.ender_eyes.title: Eye of Ender
quests.lost_light.end.the_end.desc.0: Deep within the stronghold is a portal room. Fill every empty socket in the frame with eyes, and the portal opens.
quests.lost_light.end.the_end.desc.2: The only ways back are defeating whoever waits on the other side, or dying. Take the best of everything you have.
quests.lost_light.end.the_end.subtitle: There is no way back
quests.lost_light.end.the_end.title: Beyond the Edge of the World
quests.lost_light.end.title: The End
quests.lost_light.exploration.bandits.de: Bandits set up camps and whole villages &ein the hills and plains&r, far from the king's roads.
quests.lost_light.exploration.bandits.ta: Find a bandit camp or village
quests.lost_light.exploration.buried_tre: Treasure maps are found in shipwrecks. Follow the map to &ethe coast&r and dig where X marks the spot.
quests.lost_light.exploration.castle.des: At the heart of each kingdom stands its ruler's castle. Find at least one, and decide whether you are the king's friend or foe.
quests.lost_light.exploration.dig_site.d: Ancient settlements sank under the ground. Find trail ruins or mud-brick remains and clear suspicious sand and gravel with a &6brush&r: you may find sherds for decorated pots.
quests.lost_light.exploration.dwarves.de: Dwarves live &ein the mountains and underground&r: their towers, bunkers, mines and underground villages are full of riches, and dangers.
quests.lost_light.exploration.explorer.d: The world of Lost Light is full of ruins, settlements and ancient secrets. Peoples keep to their lands: dwarves in the mountains, orcs in the badlands, human kingdoms share the plains and forests.

Quests in this chapter complete when you stand inside a structure. They unlock in a chain: tick this quest first, then find the nearby places, and the faraway ones will open. Each find gives a crate of loot, and the more dangerous the place, the richer it is.
quests.lost_light.exploration.explorer.s: Not all who wander are lost
quests.lost_light.exploration.fairy_ring: A circle of mushrooms in a glade is a sign that fairies dance here. Be polite: fairies remember both kindness and insult.
Lone houses, barns, windmills and stables stand far from villages. Their owners are used to relying only on themselves.
quests.lost_light.exploration.forts.desc: Eight kingdoms (Valaria, Bohemia, Caladria, Visgothia, Galicia, Numeria, Gardonia and Lancastia) guard their lands with forts and outposts. There are mercenaries too: the Aegis and the Gilded Legion.
quests.lost_light.exploration.forts.task: Find a fort or an outpost
quests.lost_light.exploration.giant_tree: Giant trees grow amid the forests: oaks, ashes, hickories, acacias, kapoks and plums. They say these trees remember the first days of the world, and some only pretend to be trees. Don't be hasty, nothing here is done in a hurry.
quests.lost_light.exploration.hobbit_hol: Not a damp burrow but a cosy home with a round door, full pantries and a kettle on the fire. Look for it &ein the hills&r, and wipe your feet.
A round door in a green hill
Small settlements of huts are the first homes of people. Their dwellers live just like you did at the start of your journey.
quests.lost_light.exploration.huts.subti: Simple folk of a simple age
quests.lost_light.exploration.huts.title: Huts
quests.lost_light.exploration.illagers.d: Raiders build outposts, forts, windmills and even whole mansions. Somewhere on the lakes their galleys lie at anchor.
quests.lost_light.exploration.illagers.s: Their banner is a bad omen
quests.lost_light.exploration.lighthouse: Lighthouses and fishing huts stand &eon the coast&r. From here, as from the Grey Havens, people sail out to sea: some for fish, some never to return.
Find a lighthouse or a fishing hut
Merchants set up camp &eon the plains&r on their way between settlements.
Orcs have settled &ein the badlands&r: their forts and outposts are guarded by vicious warriors. Come armed, or meat's back on the menu.
quests.lost_light.exploration.orcs.task0: Find an orc fort or outpost
quests.lost_light.exploration.orcs.title: Orc Lands
quests.lost_light.exploration.ruins.desc: Mossy fragments of walls remind of those who were here before you. Ruins can be found &ealmost anywhere&r.
quests.lost_light.exploration.shrine.des: Seven ancient gods (Argon, Esret, Gwanador, Maldor, Nessus, Typhon and Venusia) left their shrines in the world. Spirits guard them jealously.
quests.lost_light.exploration.stronghold: Deep underground lie the mazes of an ancient stronghold and an underground city. Those who built them sealed something below. Why?
quests.lost_light.exploration.sunken.des: Shipwrecks, underwater ruins and temples lie &ein the ocean&r. They say a whole island kingdom lies at the bottom, swallowed by the waves for its pride. You'll need a boat, and the ability to hold your breath.
quests.lost_light.exploration.sunken.tas: Find a shipwreck or sunken ruins
quests.lost_light.exploration.tavern.des: Taverns stand along roads and in settlements. Travellers rest here, and the innkeeper always knows what's going on nearby. Keep an eye on the quiet stranger in the corner: what if he's a ranger?
quests.lost_light.exploration.tavern.sub: A mug of ale and fresh rumours
quests.lost_light.exploration.temple.des: The pyramids of &edeserts&r and temples of &ejungles&r were built long before the kingdoms. Treasures lie beneath their floors, along with traps for the careless.
quests.lost_light.exploration.temple.tas: Find a temple or a pyramid
quests.lost_light.exploration.title: Explorer
quests.lost_light.exploration.undead.des: Crypts, dungeons and the plague asylum crawl with the undead. Bring torches, and remember where the exit is.
quests.lost_light.exploration.undead.tas: Find a crypt or a dungeon
quests.lost_light.exploration.village.de: Villages are home to villagers who trade for gems. A village's look depends on the land: dwarven in the mountains, oases in deserts, log houses in forests.
quests.lost_light.exploration.watchtower: Kingdoms watch for forest fires and enemies from these towers. Climb up and look around: you might spot something interesting.
quests.lost_light.exploration.way_sign.d: Way signs stand at crossroads and point to the nearest settlements. A good reason to hit the road.
quests.lost_light.exploration.wells.desc: Wells are the heart of any settlement. And at the bottom of some, they say, lie the coins of those who made wishes.
quests.lost_light.exploration.witches.de: Witches settle &ein swamps&r and deep forests. Cauldrons of potions bubble in their huts.
quests.lost_light.exploration.wizard_tow: Lonely wizard towers and their buried dungeons keep magical relics. Beware of traps!
quests.lost_light.farming.compost.desc.0: A &6Composter&r of lumber and dirt turns waste into the best fertilizer. It needs both &6green&r waste (plants, grain, fruit and vegetables) and &6brown&r (leaves, ash, jute, pumpkins, pinecones).
quests.lost_light.farming.compost.desc.2: Compost takes about 12 days; faster with snow on top, slower in a climate that's too dry or too wet. &cMeat and bones spoil it&r: rotten compost kills plants.
quests.lost_light.farming.compost.title: Compost
quests.lost_light.farming.fertilizers.de: Fertilizer is applied to farmland or to a crop. What each gives:
- &6guano&r (deep underground and on gravelly shores): nitrogen 80, phosphorus 50, potassium 10;
Each crop has its own &6temperature&r and &6hydration&r range: check them in the &dfield guide&r and plant for your climate. Rice grows only in water one block deep, and beans and tomatoes need a stick to climb.
There are three nutrients: &6nitrogen&r, &6phosphorus&r and &6potassium&r. Each crop loves one of them: eating it, the crop grows faster and yields more. Their levels show while holding a hoe.
quests.lost_light.farming.herbicide.desc: Rotten compost dissolved in a barrel of water becomes &6herbicide&r. In a sprinkler or an injector it burns away weeds, grass and crops.
Good for clearing a field. Bad if you mix up the barrels.
The &6Injector&r goes right on top of a filled aqueduct: it finds the farmland along the aqueduct network and feeds it. It holds 10 buckets.
Placed on a Firmalife copper pipe, it feeds the planters under that pipe's sprinklers.
quests.lost_light.farming.injector.title: Fertigation Injector
quests.lost_light.farming.liquid_fertili: Fertilizer can be dissolved in a &6barrel&r of fresh water: compost makes compost tea, bone meal makes bone extract, and guano, ash, sylvite, saltpeter and shellfish make their own solutions.
Liquid fertilizer is sprayed by sprinkler racks or carried through aqueducts by injectors.
quests.lost_light.farming.rich_soil.desc: &6Organic Compost&r is made from soil, two rich green and two rich brown waste items, rotten flesh, compost and rotten compost. The soil quality in the recipe sets the kind of compost.
Once placed, the block slowly turns into &6Rich Soil&r. Crops grow faster on it, and tilled it becomes rich farmland.
quests.lost_light.farming.rubber.desc.0: Latex boiled in a pot with sulfur sets into &6rubber&r. With Firmalife it makes sealed bricks.
quests.lost_light.farming.rubber.subtitl: If only we knew what for
quests.lost_light.farming.rubber.title: Rubber
quests.lost_light.farming.seeds.desc.0: Seeds come from &ewild crops&r: break a wild plant and you get seeds. A mature crop killed by weather or left to rot goes to seed too.
quests.lost_light.farming.seeds.desc.2: A bed needs a &6hoe&r: a stone one is knapped from rock like any other tool.
quests.lost_light.farming.seeds.subtitle: No sowing, no reaping
quests.lost_light.farming.seeds.title: Seeds
quests.lost_light.farming.sprinkler.desc: A &6Sprinkler Rack&r is built from a rack with brass mechanisms. Put an open barrel of liquid fertilizer above the nozzle, and it sprays the farmland two blocks below its base within radius 2.
Shift+right-click the nozzle to toggle it. Each extra &6rack leg&r raises the nozzle and adds 1 to the radius. Plain water won't work.
quests.lost_light.farming.syrup.desc.0: Sap is boiled down in a &6pot&r twice: first into concentrate, then into syrup. Don't forget a stick to stir, or it won't boil.
quests.lost_light.farming.syrup.desc.2: 50 buckets of maple sap make one bucket of syrup, birch sap half as much. Syrup in a jug turns into sugar.
quests.lost_light.farming.syrup.subtitle: Fifty buckets for one
quests.lost_light.farming.syrup.title: Maple Syrup
quests.lost_light.farming.title: Farming
A &6Tree Tap&r is forged from wrought iron and placed in the middle of a trunk at least three blocks tall. An open barrel goes under it.
Maple and birch give sap in spring at -4 to 6 °C, when the snow melts. Hevea gives latex above 22 °C, the rubber fig from 12 °C but slower.
quests.lost_light.farming.tree_tap.subti: The sweet tears of the maple
quests.lost_light.farming.tree_tap.title: Tree Tapping
quests.lost_light.firmalife.beekeeping.d: Place a &6beehive&r with frames near flowers, and bees will move in on their own. Combs give honey and &6beeswax&r, which you need to build a cellar.
More about beekeeping in the &dfield guide&r.
Like vessels and barrels, a &6cellar&r makes food last even longer. But a cellar is a multiblock structure and has to be built exactly as the &dfield guide&r describes.
The walls are made of &6sealed bricks&r: stone bricks coated with beeswax.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.cellar.title: Cellar
Dairy gives a bonus to &6health&r in your nutrition. Curdled milk is strained through &6cheesecloth&r, and cheese wheels age in a cellar.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.cheese.title: Cheese
quests.lost_light.firmalife.chocolate.de: Chocolate is every sweet tooth's favourite and not easy to make: cocoa beans have to be roasted, ground and mixed. And chocolate can be cast in molds, just like metal!
A &6drying mat&r woven from fruit leaves dries fruit, herbs and tobacco. Put it in the sun and wait.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.drying.subti: Let the sun do the work
quests.lost_light.firmalife.drying.title: Drying
Firmalife adds lots of fruit trees to the world. Fruit makes great jam, and leaves are woven into drying mats.
For now, just gather some leaves.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.greenhouse.d: In a &6greenhouse&r crops grow in any season and any climate. Build it from whatever you have: walls and roofs are made of glass and &6treated lumber&r (lumber with beeswax), copper rods or wrought iron rods. Types can't be mixed: the whole greenhouse must be of one type.

A greenhouse is run by a &6climate station&r: planks, brass mechanisms, redstone dust and blue glass. Planters inside are watered with a watering can. See the &dfield guide&r for how to set it all up.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.greenhouse.t: A greenhouse door of any type
quests.lost_light.firmalife.oven.desc.0: Firmalife ovens bake bread, pies and other pastries. Build one from a bottom, a hopper and a chimney, then fire it up so the clay cures. See the Firmalife section of the &dfield guide&r.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.oven.subtitl: Bread is the staff of life
quests.lost_light.firmalife.oven.title: Oven
quests.lost_light.firmalife.pineapple.de: &6Pineapples&r grow on bushes in warm climates. Besides juicy fruit, their leaves give fiber, which becomes yarn and even pineapple leather.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.planters.des: &6Planters&r grow vegetables, berries and even small trees, but they only work inside a &6greenhouse&r with a climate station. They're made of bricks and compost. See the &dfield guide&r.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.stainless_gr: Wood darkens, copper turns green, iron rusts. The greenhouse keeps working but looks worse and worse. Only &6stainless steel&r never ages: an alloy of steel, chromium and nickel, the ratios are in the &dfield guide&r.
A &6compost tumbler&r made of wrought iron sheets speeds up fertilizer production.
quests.lost_light.firmalife.title: Firmalife
Tuna and arapaima are too big for a seed on a hook. You need &6large bait&r (cod, salmon, tropical fish, bluegill or minnow), and only a &6wrought iron&r or better rod can hold it.
Big fish pull harder: hold the rod in your offhand to make it easier.
quests.lost_light.fishing.big_fish.subti: The old man and the sea
quests.lost_light.fishing.big_fish.title: The Big One
quests.lost_light.fishing.corals.desc.0: &6Corals&r grow in warm seas. A living coral cut with a knife gives dye of its color. Dead coral is ground in a quern or cut with a knife into &6coral powder&r.
quests.lost_light.fishing.corals.desc.2: The powder with limewater in a barrel becomes mortar, and in a barrel of fresh water, liquid fertilizer.
quests.lost_light.fishing.corals.title: Corals
quests.lost_light.fishing.fillet.desc.0: Aquaculture fish aren't eaten whole. Put a fish and any knife in the crafting grid to get &6fish fillet&r. The bigger the fish, the more fillets and &6fish bones&r. Bones are ground into bone meal, and large fish may yield blubber.
quests.lost_light.fishing.fillet.desc.2: Sometimes odd things are found in a big fish's belly.
quests.lost_light.fishing.fillet.title: Fillet
quests.lost_light.fishing.first_catch.de: Fish follow the climate like everything else in this world: cold seas, warm seas, rivers and lakes, dry lands and jungles. Different places, different catch.
Raw fish almost always has to be cleaned first.
quests.lost_light.fishing.fish_mount.des: The best catch deserves a wall. A &6Fish Mount&r is made from lumber and a fish hook. Put a fish on it and let your guests envy.
quests.lost_light.fishing.fish_of_the_wo: - &6cold sea&r (up to 0 °C): cod, halibut, herring, pink salmon, pollock, rainbow trout;
- &6fresh water&r (0-20 °C): perch, carp, catfish, muskellunge, minnow, brown trout;
- &6warm dry lands&r (from 13 °C, up to 300 mm of rain): bayad, boulti, capitaine, synodontis;
quests.lost_light.fishing.fishing_rod.de: First a &6fish hook&r is forged on the anvil, and a rod is made from it. Without bait it's useless: put seeds, shellfish or a &6worm&r on the hook in the crafting grid. Worms sometimes turn up when you harvest crops.
Cast and wait for a bite. Reel in smoothly: pull too fast and the fish gets away with the bait. Drag the fish ashore and finish it.
quests.lost_light.fishing.neptunian_pear: The most valuable find in a big fish's belly is a &6Neptunian Pearl&r. Clean big fish, and sooner or later one will turn up.
The pearl melts at 850 °C into the metal &6neptunium&r: three pearls make almost an ingot.
A gift from the lord of the sea
quests.lost_light.fishing.neptunium.desc: Melt pearls in a crucible or a vessel and cast a &6neptunium ingot&r in a mold. Weld it with a &6black steel&r ingot to get &6Neptunian steel&r, the metal of underwater gear.
quests.lost_light.fishing.neptunium_armo: Armor blanks are forged from a double sheet of Neptunian steel, then welded to a second such sheet. Each piece lists its effects in the tooltip.
Neptunium also makes tools and weapons, and Neptunian steel even makes buckets.
quests.lost_light.fishing.subtitle.0: Rods, catches and gifts of the sea
quests.lost_light.fishing.tackle_box.des: A &6Tackle Box&r is made from a chest, iron ingots and an iron block, plus kelp, algae or green dye. It's a handy place for bait, hooks and lines.
quests.lost_light.fishing.title: Fishing
quests.lost_light.fishing.turtles.desc.0: Along with fish, &6turtles&r get on the hook: box turtles, starshell turtles and, in jungles, arrau turtles. They make turtle soup.
quests.lost_light.fishing.turtles.title: Turtles
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.adder_sto: The fey are unseen until struck. An &6Adder Stone&r held in hand shows them at all times. They give it for any sedimentary stone once your standing reaches 40.
The higher your standing, the more they offer, but each trade spends a little of it.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.divine_co: The &6Divine Compass&r is crafted in a column: a lens, native silver ore, a bowl. Choose a god, and the needle leads to that god's nearest shrine instead of north. It never shows coordinates.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.fey_frien: Some fey can be won over. A friend follows you and fights what you fight.
- a &6Silvery String&r (standing 250, for plain string) tames a fairy;
- a &6Thicket Pact&r (standing 200, for a TFC oak log), a dryad.
The fey send a dryad only to those they hate, so meeting one is a bad sign already.
A silvery string or a thicket pact
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.fey_gifts: As your standing grows, the fey offer more:
- the &6Wildrunner Charm&r (60): for a string and a flower; undergrowth no longer slows you;
- the &6Staff of Herbs&r (100): for a stick and a flower; draws wild growth out of the soil;
- the &6Enchanted Rock&r (150): for a metamorphic rock; holds fey essence for the altar.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.full_moon: It's a full moon tonight. One night in eight the surface belongs to the spirits of light: no new shades appear, and wisps dance by still water and on mountain tops.
A good night to step outside. There aren't many of those.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.god_statu: God statues aren't made: they're found in shrine ruins. But a statue once found can be carved again: stack three blocks of that god's stone and click them holding the statue and a chisel.
The gods' stones: chalk for Esret, gabbro for Argon, basalt for Maldor, slate for Typhon, marble for Venusia, shale for Nessus, quartzite for Gwanador.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.october.d: October has come, the middle of autumn, when light and dark slip into the mortal world most easily.

Light spirits rise every night without waiting for the full moon. Shades grow stronger and press even into fey lands, and a shade caught now is a &6Cursed spirit&r worth twice the essence. The fey hide at night, and dullahans guard their ground. Only this month do the fey trade the Pumpkin Pact.
A statue takes nothing from your hands. Stand a &6Golden Brazier&r (forged from a gold double sheet) facing the statue, lay out an offering, bury it in straw and light it.

If the day is right and the god hasn't been given to yet, what burns becomes &6divine essence&r in the statue's reserve. Every god gives light essence, most also a second kind: Esret and Venusia fey, Argon and Maldor troll, Typhon and Nessus dark. Gwanador gives only light, but generously.
A &6Holy Staff&r is forged from a gold double ingot. Strike a statue with it and it charges with light, standing in for a light spirit: it wakes an altar or infuses a crucifix.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.runestone: The fey are spirits of the living wood. Their lands are marked by a ring of pale mushrooms, and the holding runs eight chunks around it. &cDon't step into the ring&r until the fey trust you: they'll seize you and drag you under.

Cutting their groves and spoiling their soil turns the fey against you, and killing fey even more so. Gifts on their ground (bones, hides, raw meat, sugar, sylvite, and precious metals most of all) raise their trust. Resentment fades slowly, and goodwill never fades.
To trade, lay items on fey ground and wait. The first thing they'll give is a &6Runestone&r, for any igneous stone: under open sky it shows how the fey regard you.
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.seven_god: Seven gods divide the week, each answering only on their own day and only once a day:
- &6Esret&r, harvest and forest, Monday: fruit, grain, vegetables;
- &6Argon&r, war, Tuesday: bones, bread, weapon metals;
- &6Maldor&r, the forge, Wednesday: fuel, metals, minerals;
- &6Typhon&r, storm and sea, Thursday: sea creatures, sea plants, shells;
- &6Venusia&r, fertility, Friday: milk and eggs, raw hides, raw meat;
- &6Gwanador&r, the sun and king, Sunday: gems, gold, silver. On his day he accepts any god's offering at half its worth.
Seven gods and the hidden folk
quests.lost_light.gods_and_fey.title: Gods and Fey
quests.lost_light.husbandry.carts.desc.0: &6Carts&r carry lots of items, chests and even animals. The best way to move house or trade.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.carts.desc.2: You can harness not only a horse, but also a donkey or a yak.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.carts.title: Carts
quests.lost_light.husbandry.eggs.desc.0: Chickens, ducks and quails lay eggs only in a &6Nest Box&r, which they find on their own. With a male around, the next egg is fertilized: its tooltip says when it will hatch.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.eggs.desc.2: Eggs are boiled and fried, and they're needed in baking too.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.eggs.title: Henhouse
Livestock is tamed with food: each animal has its favorites, look them up in the &dfield guide&r. Familiarity is shown by a heart over the animal (the key is in the field guide). Without food it slowly drops, but once the heart outline turns white, it no longer decays.

An adult can't be fully familiarized, but a baby can. Mammals mate when familiarity is above 30% and both have been fed that day, and the young are born only months later. Animals age: old ones are only good for meat.
Feed any animal up to 30% familiarity and stand next to it: the quest will complete.
The way to the heart is through the stomach
Raise an animal's familiarity to 30% and stand next to it
quests.lost_light.husbandry.horseshoes.d: Each horseshoe is forged on its own from steel or colored steel, and four are put together into a set. A shod horse runs faster: see the tooltip.
With good horseshoes a horse jumps right out of the usual safety pit, so better tie it up.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.mob_net.desc: A &6Mob Net&r catches livestock: birds, or the young of larger animals. A caught animal can be carried in your inventory and released somewhere new.
A grown cow won't fit in a net: it's too large.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.name_tag.des: Name tags aren't made: they're found &ein the chests of ruins and dungeons&r. Give a name to your favorite animal.
A horse, donkey or mule can be ridden once familiarity reaches 15%. A &6Saddle&r is cut from leather. Donkeys and mules carry a chest or a barrel.
Two can share a saddle: take a companion along.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.saddle.title: Saddle
quests.lost_light.husbandry.shearing.des: Sheep, alpacas and musk oxen grow &6wool&r. A tamed adult can be sheared with &6shears&r. Alpacas regrow it fastest, musk oxen slowest, but they live longer.
Wool is spun into yarn on a spindle, and a loom turns yarn into cloth.
Small stables stand &eon the plains&r. Look inside: there may be something for your steed.
quests.lost_light.husbandry.stable.title: The Stable
quests.lost_light.husbandry.title: Husbandry
quests.lost_light.kitchen.baking.desc.0: Bread and pies from a Firmalife oven keep longer: oven-baked food decays a tenth slower.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.baking.title: Fresh from the Oven
quests.lost_light.kitchen.brining.desc.0: Soak food in a barrel of &6brine&r (one part vinegar to nine parts salt water), then seal it in a barrel of &6vinegar&r to get pickles that keep for a very long time. Vinegar is made in a barrel: a fruit and 250 mB of alcohol.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.brining.title: Brine and Pickles
quests.lost_light.kitchen.cooking_pot.de: A &6cooking pot&r makes stews, soups, pasta and desserts. Put it on a fire or a &6stove&r, add ingredients and wait. The pot is welded from metal sheets on an anvil.
On a &6cutting board&r a knife turns meat into mince and bacon, fish into fillets and vegetables into slices. Put food on the board and right-click it with a knife.
Any TFC knife will do, even a stone one.
A sharp knife is half the job
quests.lost_light.kitchen.drying_food.de: Dry fruit or herbs on a &6drying mat&r in the sun. Dried fruit weighs little and lasts long: the best supply for a long road.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.feast.desc.0: Guests arrived unannounced, and they're all hungry. Make a feast dish: roast chicken, honey-glazed ham, shepherd's pie or stuffed pumpkin. Put it on the table and every guest cuts a serving.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.feast.subtitle: Thirteen dwarves for dinner
quests.lost_light.kitchen.feast.title: An Unexpected Party
Food cooked on a grill over a firepit keeps longer than usual: 1.66 times against 1.33 for a plain firepit. Grill something.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.grilling.title: Over the Coals
quests.lost_light.kitchen.jam.desc.0: Cook fruit or berries with sugar in a pot and pour them into glass jars. A sealed jar of jam never spoils, and jam spread on bread turns it into a sandwich.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.jam.subtitle: Summer in a jar
quests.lost_light.kitchen.jam.title: Jam
quests.lost_light.kitchen.pasta.desc.0: Cut dough on the board to get raw pasta. Cook it in the pot with meatballs, mutton or vegetables.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.pasta.subtitle: Dough, a knife and some patience
quests.lost_light.kitchen.pasta.title: Pasta
Pemmican is a mix of dried meat, fat and berries. It barely spoils and is perfect for long journeys. One piece keeps you walking for half a day.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.pemmican.subti: Not lembas, but filling all the same
quests.lost_light.kitchen.pemmican.title: Pemmican
quests.lost_light.kitchen.rotten.desc.0: There's no mistaking the smell: something in your inventory has rotted. Food spoils in this world, and raw meat and fish go first.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.rotten.desc.2: Rot is still good for compost, but don't eat it. Here's some salt, so it happens less often.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.rotten.task0: Let food rot in your inventory
quests.lost_light.kitchen.rotten.title: Something Died in Here
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salad.desc.0: A fresh vegetable or fruit salad is a quick way to boost fruit and vegetables in your diet. Add Survivor's Delight dressing for taste.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salad.subtitle: Vitamins for the traveller
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salad.title: Salad
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salting.desc.0: Fresh meat goes bad in a few days. Sprinkle it with &6salt&r on a crafting grid and it keeps much longer. Salt comes from halite or from evaporated seawater.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salting.desc.2: TFC shows every preservation method in the food tooltip. See the food preservation section of the &dfield guide&r.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salting.subtit: Salt is the gold of the kitchen
quests.lost_light.kitchen.salting.title: Salting
A sandwich combines the nutrition of all its ingredients and can keep longer than they would separately. Put meat, cheese or vegetables between two slices of bread, or spread some jam.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.sandwich.title: Sandwich
quests.lost_light.kitchen.skillet.desc.0: A &6skillet&r fries right over the fire, or in your hand once heated on a stove. Survivor's Delight adds skillets of TFC metals: copper, bronze, steel…
quests.lost_light.kitchen.skillet.desc.2: You can also whack an enemy with it. Dwarf-tested.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.skillet.title: Skillet
quests.lost_light.kitchen.smoking.desc.0: Firmalife lets you smoke meat and cheese. Brine meat in a barrel first; cheese can go straight in. Place &6wool string&r within four blocks above a firepit and hang the food on it: in 8 hours it will be smoked.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.smoking.desc.2: Burn only logs in the firepit: peat makes the food disgusting.
quests.lost_light.kitchen.smoking.title: Smokehouse
quests.lost_light.kitchen.stew.desc.0: Cook a thick stew or a soup in the pot. What's a journey without a hot stew by the fire?
quests.lost_light.kitchen.stew.subtitle: Boil 'em, mash 'em, stick 'em in a stew
quests.lost_light.kitchen.stew.task0: Any stew or soup from the pot
quests.lost_light.kitchen.stew.title: Stew
quests.lost_light.kitchen.title: Kitchen
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.black_steel: Alloy steel, nickel and black bronze into &6weak steel&r, then weld its ingot with a pig iron ingot on an anvil to get &6high carbon black steel&r. Working it on a steel anvil gives a black steel ingot, the material of the best tools before blue and red steel.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.blasting.de: A &6plunger&r fires all linked charges at once, and &6quarry dynamite&r doesn't destroy rock but turns it into rubble, so the mine doesn't cave in. A blasting cap switches a stick to tunnel mode.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.channel_cas: A crucible can pour into several molds at once. Knap &6channels&r and &6mold tables&r from clay, fire them and connect the crucible to the tables with channels. Shift-right-click a table to place a mold, and right-click the channel next to the crucible to start pouring.
Bellows next to a table cool the metal faster. A channel can also be opened with a redstone pulse.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.crude_cruci: A crucible is expensive, but alloys are needed already in the Bronze Age. In Lost Light a plain ceramic &6vessel&r works as a crude crucible: you can mix molten metals in it and pour the alloy into molds.
Make do with what you have
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.dynamite.de: The compound is rolled into &6dynamite sticks&r. A stick attaches to a block face; embedded in stone, it blasts much harder. Sticks are linked with &6fuse cord&r and lit from one end with a firestarter.
The spark doesn't travel instantly: be somewhere else when it arrives.
A blast furnace needs thick walls of fire bricks. &6Insulation&r made of wrought iron sheets and flux gives &6insulated fire bricks&r, so the furnace can be built more compactly.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.mineral_pro: Tired of finding metal while looking for kaolin or graphite? A &6mineral prospector&r only notices minerals (gypsum, kaolin, graphite, sulfur and others) in a 45×45×45 cube.
A mineral prospector of any metal
A charcoal forge can be made bigger: lay a square of charcoal piles up to 3×3, at least 7 layers in each space, and light it. It works as a single forge but heats several items and crucibles at once, and bellows fan it as a whole. It doesn't need open sky.
Tick the quest when you've built yours.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.nitroglycer: Sulfur and water give &6sulfuric acid&r, with saltpeter &6nitric acid&r, and a mix of both acids with &6glycerol&r (lye and fat or olive oil) gives unstable nitroglycerin. Seal the barrel and let it settle: touch the barrel too soon and it explodes.
Stable nitroglycerin is absorbed into dried mud brick powder to make a &6stable compound&r.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.ore_washing: Grind ore in a quern to get &6dirty powder&r. Wash it in a barrel of water and you get clean ore powder. Four powders make a &6pile&r, four piles a &6pellet&r: it holds 80 mB of metal and takes the space of a single ore piece.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.prospector_: A &6prospector's drill&r looks deep: it checks a 7×25×7 strip in the direction of the face you hit. Handy when you know a vein is near but not where. The head is forged from a tuyere.
A prospector's drill of any metal
A prospector's pick searches too widely. A &6prospector's hammer&r checks only a 13×13×13 cube around the block you hit: if it finds ore, the ore is close by.
The head is cast in a clay mold or forged from a double ingot.
A prospector's hammer of any metal
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.saltpeter.d: Saltpeter ore dissolves in a barrel of water into &6crude niter solution&r. Boil 1000 mB of it in a pot with a pinch of wood ash and &6saltpeter crystals&r are left, which you grind into powder. This yields much more than grinding the ore.
You can also get the solution without ore: seal humus, compost or guano in a barrel of water.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.smith_secre: Forging in TFC is a minigame: you hit the target while doing the last strikes in the right order. In Lost Light the anvil helps: the remaining steps are shown beside the forging screen, and welding has its own button.
Try welding two ingots into a &6double ingot&r: anvils, prospecting tools and much more are forged from them.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.thermal_min: Around &evolcanoes and hot springs&r rare minerals form: apatite, calcite, smithsonite, brimstone and more. They are used for chemistry, fertilizers and dyes. Be careful: a volcano sometimes throws red-hot bombs.
quests.lost_light.metallurgy.title: Metallurgy
quests.lost_light.relics.artifact.desc.0: &6Artifacts&r are old items with magical properties: rings, amulets, belts, daggers, staves, armor. Each has its own abilities, shown in the tooltip.
quests.lost_light.relics.artifact.desc.2: Look for them in the chests of &ewizard towers, dungeons and ancient temples&r. Towers are guarded by traps: crumbling floors, hidden dispensers and tripwires.
quests.lost_light.relics.artifact.title: An Artifact
quests.lost_light.relics.curios.desc.0: Rings, amulets and belts aren't held in hand: they go into &6trinket slots&r. Open your inventory and find the Curios slots button.
quests.lost_light.relics.curios.desc.2: Trinkets have weight too, so don't put on everything you find.
quests.lost_light.relics.curios.subtitle: Wear it
quests.lost_light.relics.curios.title: Trinkets
Legendary rings (health, satiety, luck and regeneration) are very rare. And the mythic rings of flight and undying have been seen by a handful.
Don't put the ring on if it starts whispering.
quests.lost_light.relics.manaessence.des: An unwanted artifact breaks down into four pieces of &6raw manaessence&r. Raw manaessence with a gold nugget and a material (wood, leather, stone, iron, gold or diamond) becomes manaessence of that material.
quests.lost_light.relics.ring.desc.0: &6Rings of Ascension&r give a constant effect while worn: night vision, a high jump, water walking and much more. They're found &ein the chests of dungeons, mines, pyramids, ships and buried treasure&r.
quests.lost_light.relics.ring.desc.2: Rings are common, rare, epic, legendary and mythic: the rarer the ring, the stronger.
quests.lost_light.relics.ring.subtitle: One ring…
quests.lost_light.relics.ring.title: Ring of Ascension
quests.lost_light.relics.title: Relics and Rings
quests.lost_light.relics.totem.desc.0: A &6Totem of Undying&r saves you from death once. It's carried by &eevokers&r, the illager sorcerers of woodland mansions.
quests.lost_light.relics.totem.desc.2: You don't have to hold the totem: put it in the &6charm&r slot, and it works by itself.
quests.lost_light.relics.totem.subtitle: A second chance
quests.lost_light.relics.totem.title: Totem of Undying
quests.lost_light.seafaring.abandoned_sh: On &ecoasts&r and in &eswamps&r you may find unfinished rowboats and sloops, left by owners who never came back. See how the hull is built: it makes building your own easier.
Cannons are mounted on big ships and on land: the best tool against enemy vessels. The barrel is forged from wrought iron double sheets, cannonballs from double ingots.
Firing takes gunpowder, paper and a flint and steel. You can adjust the barrel angle in place.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.cannon.title: Cannons
quests.lost_light.seafaring.rigging.desc: A sailing ship needs ropes and sails. A &6rope coil&r is woven from jute, and sails are sewn from wool cloth.
Sails can be dyed any color, each one separately.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.rowboat.desc: The rowboat is the first real ship of the Iron Age: three seats, and even a horse fits.

Place the scaffolding in a 2×3 rectangle facing inward, cover it with planks and bolts, then set &6oarlocks&r forged from wrought iron double ingots in the middle and fit the &6oars&r. The rower sits facing backwards, to really put their back into it.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.shipwright.d: Big boats aren't crafted but built in place. Their base is &6shipwright's scaffolding&r: flat and angled frames placed in the shape of the future hull.
Each frame takes four planks of a strong hardwood, nailed with &6copper bolts&r while holding a hammer in your offhand. Bolts are forged from copper.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.shipwright.s: First the frame, then the ship
quests.lost_light.seafaring.sloop.desc.0: The sloop is a true ship of the Steel Age: four blocks wide, over eight long, up to seven passengers, thirteen containers and six cannons.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.sloop.desc.2: It's expensive: steel, copper, hundreds of lumber, cloth and jute. First the hull of scaffolding with flat frames, then &6cleats&r of steel double ingots. The rest is built in place following the blue hammer hints.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.sloop.desc.4: Sailing is a skill: catch the wind, set the sails at the right angle, and drop the &6anchor&r by the shore.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.sloop.subtit: The Straight Road to the West
quests.lost_light.seafaring.sloop.title: Sloop
quests.lost_light.seafaring.timepiece.de: A sextant finds your latitude, and a &6navigator's timepiece&r your longitude: it keeps the time of the prime meridian. Together they give exact coordinates anywhere in the world.
One degree is about 222 blocks. The timepiece body is forged from a brass double sheet.
quests.lost_light.seafaring.timepiece.su: Where am I? How many degrees from home?
quests.lost_light.seafaring.title: Seafaring
quests.lost_light.spirits.altar_gifts.de: Gem powder becomes glowstone dust for 10 light essence, and an apple with a gold ingot becomes a golden apple for 25 light.
The altar also enchants weapons and tools:
- a blade with a &6black bronze&r ingot for 100 dark essence: Sharpness II;
- a blade with a &6silver&r ingot for 50 light: Smite IV;
- a tool with gem powder for 100 troll: Efficiency II.
quests.lost_light.spirits.altar_gifts.ta: A golden apple or glowstone dust from the altar
quests.lost_light.spirits.earth_staffs.d: Each staff changes the land around it:
- the &6Staff of Decay&r (stick and ash, 100 dark): kills grass, crops and leaves. &cThe fey won't forgive it on their ground&r;
- the &6Staff of Moss&r (stick and moss, 5 fey): spreads moss over cobble and bricks;
- the &6Rock Melting Staff&r (sulfur and four igneous rocks, 80 troll): melts cobble back into raw rock, and gravel into cobble;
- the &6Stalactite Staff&r (gypsum and limestone, 70 troll): grows stalactites and stalagmites.
The same soul glass batch, worked with copper, soda ash and graphite, is blown into an &6Evil Eye Talisman&r. Held in either hand, it strips curses at once (wither, weakness, slowness, mining fatigue, nausea and blindness) and wears a little each time.
quests.lost_light.spirits.evil_eye.title: The Evil Eye
quests.lost_light.spirits.greater_seal.d: A &6Greater Spirit Seal&r is cut at the altar: a regular seal in the center, stone (not sedimentary) around it, 100 troll essence. It holds eight spirits, but of one kind only: whatever goes in first locks it until it's empty.
Only the top spirit is spent; right-click cycles the stack.
quests.lost_light.spirits.holy_water.des: The simplest ritual: put a container of water in the center. For 5 light essence the water becomes &6holy water&r, for 5 dark, &6death water&r.
quests.lost_light.spirits.pearl_eye.desc: The &6Pearl Eye&r is made from a mollusk, ash and bones for 50 dark essence. Hold it and look at a totem or a statue to learn which spirits are inside.
There's no recipe: hold a knife in your main hand and a seal in your offhand and strike a standing log. Any of TFC's twenty woods will do.
